result.killer: No killer confirmed. The likely killer is the free or fee-based state CRBE electronic form and portal (Art. 21 and 29 of Lei 7/26), with assisted filing at registry offices. It has not been launched; the regulation was still pending as of the latest sources.
result.reason: I found nothing that kills the idea. No private CRBE software exists, and the law (Art. 2) covers sole traders, associations and cooperatives. Lei 7/26 took effect on publication, with 180 days for existing entities (to about 15 Feb 2027 per CMS), annual confirmation by 31 March and 15-day updates. Art. 18 lets certified accountants and lawyers file. But the core submission is a state electronic form (Art. 21), with assisted filing at registry offices, plus a regulated fee. The regulation, form and portal were still unpublished, so the deadline may slip. What's left for a founder is a thin layer: tracking ownership chains and deadlines for accountant portfolios. One correction: sanctions start only after the transition period (Art. 57). Art. 43(3)'s 180 days covers paying fines.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K02; no search spent (known idea). Side find: Decreto Presidencial 49/25 (foreign non-resident workers) and 50/25 (new labour-offence fines) raise exposure for any employer, but they are not household-specific.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Executive decree reported by Ver Angola on 7 Jan 2026 bans scrap yards and metal weighing houses and revokes all their licences. Steel mills and other licensed industrial users are excluded and must prove their raw material is lawfully sourced. Earlier years had annual zero-quota scrap export bans by ministerial despacho (2016-2018). The buyer group is gone, so I rejected it.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Angolan rule on pawnbrokers or second-hand/used-phone registers surfaced. Only the 2024 vendor-card regime (see K09) and a single used-goods shop (Lafitte, 2020). Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: ANRM was created in 2020 (DP 161/20 per trade.gov) and oversees mineral commercialisation. Gold buying is mostly informal, with Congolese traders; one source says occasional sale is lawful but street trading is not. I found no register or periodic report for jewellers, and the 2017 gold-trading contracts with four firms may be outdated. Nothing found.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Decreto Presidencial 165/10 sets the environmental regime for end-of-life road vehicles, covering dismantling and treatment operators. I could not read its text, so licensing and reporting duties for scrapyards and parts dealers are unconfirmed. The Jan 2026 scrap-weighing ban may hit these yards. Candidate recorded as unverified.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Animal Health Law and Decreto 70/08 (its regulation) include inspection of live-animal markets and fairs. I did not find the movement-permit rules or any digital tool. Candidate recorded as unverified.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Decreto 70/08 mentions a fresh-meat salubrity certificate. I found no Angolan butcher licensing text or register in the results (Portugal and Cabo Verde results were not usable). Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No search spent: budget went to higher-signal categories, and I had no indication of a regulatory duty.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: The search returned no Angolan clinic-licensing or veterinary-medicine register text. Only generic veterinary-authority definitions in DP 104/15 and the old 1987 sanitary regulation turned up. Unverified, no candidate.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water-use licensing rests on DP 82/14 (general water-use regulation), and DP 41/21 sets an abstraction fee regime. I did not confirm borehole or driller licensing rules, thresholds or the issuing body. Unverified.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: The new national waste regulation (VdAtlas flash) requires a waste management plan approved by the Environment Minister (valid 4 years) and an annual register of quantities transported. Septic-tank emptying firms in Luanda are licensed and inspected by the provincial government (GPL), per an O País report and a Chevron tender. Recorded as a weak candidate.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Only Portuguese, Macau and Brazilian lift rules surfaced; I found no Angolan lift or pressure-equipment inspection regime. Unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: The community water management model (MoGeCA) uses water-sanitation groups (GAS) and consumer associations (ACAS) around public standpipes, with reported lack of service contracts. A tariff regulation exists, but I found no per-system reporting duty. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Only Executive Decree 133/19 (phytosanitary certificate and import licence forms) was found, which concerns trade, not retail dealers. No retail or applicator licensing register found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: DP 51/25 sets a licence for temporary-work agencies (MAPTSS grants it, INEFOP analyses it, labour inspection checks, valid 24 months). The decree also limits temp work to the same conditions as fixed-term contracts. About 120 online employment agencies report to INEFOP (2023). DP 49/25 caps non-resident foreign workers at 30% and ties contracts to the visa, and DP 50/25 raises fines. Candidates recorded.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Only DP 178/22 (licensing and inspection of cremation establishments) was found. No general funeral or cemetery licensing text. Tiny market.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Lei 2/26 (2 March 2026) replaced the NGO regime in DP 74/15. NGOs now need administrative habilitation and enrolment with a supervisory body (ISAC per one source), must keep organised accounts, report projects, funding and transactions regularly, and face suspension of up to 120 days. About 400 NGOs; adaptation window of 180 days (late Aug or Sept 2026), which has passed. Associations with their own legal regime are excluded. Churches not confirmed. Halal and kosher: nothing found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: DP 123/22 regulates motorcycle, tricycle and quadricycle taxis. It requires a professional card, training, a vehicle licence valid 2 years, and municipal quotas set every 2 years. Luanda licensed only about 5,000 of an expected 18,000. Cooperatives complained in 2024 that no one had a card yet. Ride-hailing apps T'leva, Kubinga and Anda exist but are not compliance tools. Taxi cooperatives, minibus and trucking not examined in depth.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Street vendors: nothing new beyond K09; the 2024 regulation covers the vendor card, the licensing platform and vending bans. Money changers: Lei 14/21 governs non-bank financial institutions, BNA supervises 26 exchange houses (2023), with a 50m Kz minimum capital norm and repeated licence revocations. The pool is small and the buyers are capitalised firms. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: K04, not rechecked. Nurseries: the search found no Angolan licensing rules; preschool is private and not compulsory. Tattoo, hunting and food producers not searched, so not_reached for those sub-groups.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Regime: Lei 28/11 (petroleum products), DP 173/13 (station and storage licensing), DP 208/19 (IRDP), Decreto Executivo 80/15 (LPG filling safety). New: DP 209/24 (butane licence regulation): IRDP licenses bulk and wholesale resellers, municipal administrations license retail resellers; 5-year licence conditional on annual inspection; fines in minimum wages; no periodic reporting and no transition deadline in the text. About 898 stations at Sept 2024. 2026 press: expired and leaking cylinders in circulation, regulator oversight called weak. Candidate C1 added. Station-level reporting duties to IRDP not found.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Coffee: exporter must register with the trade ministry and INCA and hold at least 20 t of commercial coffee in store; a new decree sets an annual export campaign (1 Oct to 30 Sep), a 3-year age cap and large-lot/small-lot exporter classes (weak candidate C8). Wholesale/warehouse rules in DP 289/10 (currency unverified). Importers of pork, chicken, rice, sugar and tilapia must buy 20% from national producers to get an import licence (C9). Nothing found for maize millers or MINAGRIF grain-warehouse registration.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: BNA 2023 package: Aviso 4/23 (setting up microcredit companies and cooperative credit companies, registering microcredit operators), Aviso 5/23 (minimum capital, 1M Kz for cooperative credit companies), Aviso 7/23 (activities and information reporting of cooperative credit companies). Aviso 8/23 account database may cover some mutual credit institutions (unconfirmed for cooperatives). No 2025 cooperative-specific rule found. Candidate C10 (unverified). Text of Aviso 7/23 not read.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Could not find the licensing decree for private health units or any ERSA or ARSEG provider register. A 2019 Health Ministry statement said provisional licences are no longer issued for health units and pharmacies, and that inspections were being cut from three to one. ARSEG fined insurers heavily in 2025 (Sol Seguros 100M Kz), but no provider-billing duty was found. Health technical institutes with expired licences may not enrol students from 2025-26 (education, see 34). Nothing candidate-worthy found; insurer billing and licence renewal not checked.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: No search spent here (budget went to other categories). Known idea K03 (controlled-medicine register and ARMED maps) covers pharmacies. Only incidental find: 2019 Health Ministry comment that licensing of pharmacies and health units is being shortened to one inspection. Precursor and controlled-chemical users not checked.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security: Lei 2014, DP 225/17 regulation, DP 4/22 (training centres under police supervision), 2021 order to swap war weapons for defence weapons; no 2024-25 reporting rule found. Temporary work: DP 51/25 tightens temporary work, only licensed agencies may assign workers. INEFOP licenses private employment agencies (about 120) and they report periodically to it. Expatriate regime DP 49/25 (see C4). Candidates C4 and C5.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Oil and gas local content: DP 271/20; ANPG keeps a supplier directory, and only Angolan-owned or part-Angolan-owned firms on the ANPG database get exclusivity and preference lists. Contracts of USD 54.4bn from 2022 to 2025, about 97% to Angola-registered firms. Candidate C7 (weak). Construction site registers and quarry or mining licensing were not searched.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Real estate agents, notaries, registrars and lawyers are covered entities under the AML system (DP 35/11 under the old Lei 12/10; the current law is believed to be Lei 5/20, unverified). The UIF says over 98% of suspicious-transaction reports come from banks, and the 2022 UIF report lists lawyers as having indicators. Government is passing further laws to exit the FATF grey list. New: Lei 7/26 of 19 Aug 2026 creating the beneficial-owner register (CRBE), with 180 days for existing companies and fines up to 50M Kz (C2). Insurance mediators: Norma Regulamentar 7/25 and Aviso 2/21 (C3). AML toolkit for non-bank entities is C6 (unverified). The goAML channel and the reporting deadline were not confirmed.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Tourism enterprises are licensed under DP 36/16 (DNQIPT); one-star hotels moved to municipal administrations under decentralisation; digital licensing platform launched 2022 (servicos.minfin.gov.ao per the press report). Local accommodation must be registered with the municipal administration, with a plate, to be marketed for tourism. The foreigners-law regulation requires an accommodation declaration (boletim de alojamento) with a copy of the travel document. Candidate C11 (unverified). No tourism levy or guest-register portal found.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Angola finished the national ePhyto system (GENS/UNICC/IPPC); first ePhyto-certified container, avocados to the EU via the Lobito Corridor, due 25 Nov 2025. Temporary export ban on lemons in April 2025. Coffee export rules (see 22). Nothing found on timber or fish export licences or the forestry institute's role. EU-linked horticulture exporters are possible buyers, but ePhyto is a state system; weak lead only.

coverage.category: 31. Beneficial-owner register (Lei 7/26) - all companies and entities without legal personality
coverage.found: Lei 7/26 of 19 Aug 2026 creates the CRBE; existing entities have 180 days; fines up to 50M Kz (press, unverified against the gazette); banks and insurers must check the register. Which body runs it and how filing works were not yet defined in the press report. Candidate C2.

coverage.category: 32. Insurance mediators and brokerage (ARSEG)
coverage.found: 4,963 individual and 75 collective mediators registered in 2025. Norma Regulamentar 7/25 of 11 Aug 2025 sets new access and registration documents; Aviso 2/21 covers periodic mandatory information; ARSEG proposed mandatory civil-liability insurance for brokers (10-200M Kz, was in consultation); earlier press: 26 mediation firms stopped operating for not updating their licence and 17 brokers and 9 agents were revoked. RandTech's Anybroker app manages portfolios but no ARSEG reporting link was found. Candidate C3.

coverage.category: 33. Gambling, betting and social games (Lei 17/24, ISJ)
coverage.found: Lei 17/24 of 28 Oct 2024 replaces Lei 5/16 and covers casinos, game rooms, social games and online. The ISJ says at least 14 firms hold active licences and 6 expired; the ISJ is blocking unlicensed online platforms (1xBet, PalancaBet 2026). Licensees are few and not quiet small firms; DP 131/20 (online) and DP 141/17 (land-based) may be superseded. Candidate C12 (weak). Small betting shops and bingo halls not checked.

coverage.category: 34. Private schools, colleges and training institutes (licensing)
coverage.found: Press (2021/22): over 2,000 of 3,753 private schools in Luanda operated illegally and would not be closed; their documents were not yet in the Diário da República. 2025 joint health and education decree: technical health institutes with no licence or an expired one cannot enrol students from 2025-26; nursing and clinical-analysis courses suspended for 5 years in several provinces including Luanda. Candidate C13.

coverage.category: 35. Employers of foreign (non-resident) workers: contract registration and quota (DP 49/25)
coverage.found: DP 49/25 of 18 Feb 2025 replaces DP 43/17 and 79/17: 70:30 local to foreign quota, expatriate contracts to be registered with the employment centre within 30 days, registration fee reported as 5% of total contract salary (unverified), occupational qualifier submitted to the labour inspectorate (older Decree 70/01, unverified). Candidate C4.

coverage.category: 36. Complaints book and economic inspection (ANIESA)
coverage.found: DP 234/16 requires a complaints book with a seal in every business supplying goods or services to final consumers. DP 144/26 (reported July 2026) extinguishes INADEC and moves the complaints-book system, physical or electronic, to ANIESA, which becomes the only economic inspection body. No mandatory e-book diploma found. Candidate C14 (weak).

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No beekeeping licence, apiary or hive-registration duty found for Angola (several searches; only UNCTAD/EU honey-value-chain material from 2018-2021 and the Associação dos Apicultores de Angola, IDF as promoting body). Inspectors may demand proof and send samples to labs. The page shows no registration, record or traceability duty, and the annex wording conflicts with the mandatory text. The sector is tiny, informal and donor-funded, so willingness to pay is low. coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pharmacies: nothing new beyond K03, but Lei 4/99 (angolex) adds firm detail for the K03 build. Pharmacists must keep a special register of dispensed Table I-IV prescriptions closed each 31 Dec; keep duplicate prescriptions 3 years; send a duplicate of each narcotic or psychotropic prescription to the DNM by the 15th of the following month; verify buyer ID; report loss or theft at once. Wholesalers keep entry and exit books (closed 31 Dec, kept 3 years) and a pharmacist must be responsible for each branch. Licensing: Decreto Presidencial 41/24 (SIMPLIFICA 2.0 reform) covers pharmacies, herbalists, cosmetics and health-product shops, distributors and importers (inspection within 30 days, authorisation within 3 working days after the technical commission's opinion). The annual inspection certificate costs Kz 25,000 for pharmacies and Kz 80,000 for importers and distributors (joint executive decree; Decreto Executivo Conjunto 1/25 of 14 Jan 2025 on ARMED fees may have changed this, unchecked). SIREMA, ARMED's digital medicine-registration system, launched June 2024. No national e-prescription or traceability platform found. Pharmacies are also pulled into the AGT e-invoicing rollout (full coverage 2027), which is the rejected K05 area. Precursor and controlled-chemical users: Lei 4/99 Arts. 38-42 require authorisation from the Direcção Nacional da Indústria for production and from the Direcção Nacional do Comércio for each import or export, plus stock limits and reporting of suspicious operations. It sets no precursor register or periodic report, and the buyer group is tiny. No 2024-2027 precursor decree found. Unchecked: whether Lei 4/99 is still in force unamended, the actual current form of the monthly DNM report, whether ARMED has since replaced the DNM duty, the precursor tables and the list of authorised users.

result.competitor: I found no private software or productised service in Portuguese searches for CRBE or beneficiário efectivo filing and services. The law itself names a CRBE electronic portal. It will be a state tool, probably free, though fees are not stated. Once live, it handles the core submission, which leaves room only for advisory work, ownership-chain mapping, document collection and deadline tracking for accountant portfolios. Law firms (PLMJ, Miranda, CMS) are already marketing advisory work on the regime. Banks already collect beneficial-owner data under BNA Instrutivo 08/24.
result.duty: Lei n.º 7/26 of 19 Aug 2026 (RJBE) took effect on publication. Legal persons and entities without legal personality must keep an internal beneficial-owner record and file an initial declaration with the CRBE. Existing entities have 180 days; counted from 19 Aug 2026 this ends around 15 Feb 2027 (my calculation). Changes are due within 15 days of the event, and an annual confirmation is due by 31 March. Declarations can be filed by directors, lawyers with powers, certified accountants (for some filings) or an agent. Coverage (per Miranda): commercial companies, branches, associations, foundations, NGOs, cooperatives, unions, consortia, trusts. Excluded: state bodies, state-owned enterprises, professional associations. I could not confirm whether sole traders are covered. Penalties: daily penalties of Kz 20k per day for natural persons and Kz 200k per day for entities; fines up to Kz 50M for very serious infringements by companies; disqualification of officers; striking off the CRBE; criminal liability for false declarations. Banks and other obliged entities must check the register, so non-compliance can block banking relationships. Gaps: implementing regulations are not yet approved and no managing authority is designated, so the portal is not yet live. The gazette text was not read; I relied on PLMJ, Miranda and the Expansão summaries.
result.market: INE census (REMPE 2019): 83,722 enterprises, about 90% active. FUE 2015: about 140k companies constituted, of which only about 41.5k were active. The GUE registered 36,734 new companies in 2024 and 14,553 in Q1 2025. Associations, cooperatives and NGOs come on top of that. Realistically there are tens of thousands of active filers, but many are inactive or informal, and an Expansão-cited study says 75% never complete AGT registration.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. Lei 7/26 was published and took effect on 19 Aug 2026. Existing entities have 180 days from publication, which I calculate ends around 15 Feb 2027. Changes must be filed within 15 days and confirmed every year by 31 March. Fines reach Kz 50M, plus daily penalties of Kz 200k for legal persons. Banks must check the register. The scope is wide: companies, associations, cooperatives, NGOs. Directors, lawyers or certified accountants can file. I found no private product. But the register's managing authority and implementing regulations are still pending. Filing will go through the free state CRBE electronic portal, and existing law firms will likely take the advisory work. That leaves a thin layer of filing help and deadline reminders, aimed at accountants.

Duty is real: Lei 2/26 (2 Mar 2026) applies to all NGOs. It requires habilitation (letter, registry certificate, activity programme; 15-day decision), "periodic reports" on projects (art. 17, with no fixed frequency), external audits, and a 180-day adaptation window (art. 35, extendable once). Sanctions are suspension for 120 days, loss of support and criminal liability. No monetary fines. No NGO-specific software was found, but I did not search for competitors separately. The supervisory body is not named in the law text; press says ISAC. Weak points: reporting is vague and mostly one-off or occasional, there are no fines, buyers have little money, and the political risk is high. Market is about 400 NGOs, per the claim's Ver Angola citation, which I did not verify. Associative and foundation bodies with their own legal regime are excluded; churches are not mentioned.

The duty is real. Decreto Presidencial 123/22 of 30 May 2022 is Angolan law (DR I Série n.º 97). It requires a professional card and a vehicle licensed by the local administration. No competing licence or fleet-compliance software turned up. But I did not read the decree text, so the 2-year renewal, the quotas and the penalties are unchecked. The card was still not being issued in March 2024, and I found no 2025-26 news, so the workflow may not run yet. Buyers are low-income riders and loosely organised cooperatives, so willingness to pay is weak. The market is about 20,000+ riders in Luanda (AMOTRANG's 2023 claim). The workflow is mostly paperwork at a government counter, so there is little for software to do. Score stays at 3.

The duty is real. BNA Aviso 4/23 (28 Jun 2023) sets authorisation for cooperative credit companies and registration for microcredit operators, who are capped at Kz 250,000 per client. Aviso 7/23 (6 Jul 2023) sets information-reporting duties for cooperatives, with the terms left to a separate BNA instrument. I did not find that instrument, so the reporting frequency, the penalty and the channel are unverified. The market is tiny. Press reports cite about 1 authorised cooperative, 22 microcredit companies and 25 non-financial microcredit providers (undated). That is too few buyers for a solo founder to sell a reporting desk to. I did not search for competing software or a BNA portal, so competition is unchecked.

Duty is real: DP 108/11 art. 4 requires hotels, pensions and similar to report non-resident foreign guests to SME within 24h, with a boletim and passport copy, plus a daily guest map. The fine is under Lei 2/07 art. 103, which Lei 13/19 has since replaced, so the current penalty and whether DP 108/11 survives are unverified. Local accommodation must register with the municipal administration and display a plate (DP 78/26 amending DP 36/16). A 5% tourist levy on foreigners' stays (DPL 4/26) is new, but it is a tax rather than the guest-register workflow. No online SME channel or Angola-specific guest-register tool found; the only local PMS found (Digitalub, Odoo) does not mention it. Weak: small, informal, low-tech buyers, paper-based and thinly enforced; best as a PMS add-on.

The 2025 joint decree is confirmed only for health technical institutes (Ver Angola, Aug 2025): no enrolment from 2025-26 with a missing or expired licence. I found no evidence it covers private colleges or schools generally. Decreto Presidencial 162/23 gave schools 36 months (to about Aug 2026) to conform, which is a real one-off deadline. Luanda 2021/22 data: over 2,000 of 3,753 private schools unlicensed. ANEP claims 6,200+ colleges. I found no dedicated licence-renewal software, only generic school-management apps such as QBinary. I did not confirm the decree number, fees or renewal cycle. The core barrier is infrastructure and cost, not paperwork, and buyers are fragmented and weak payers. Budget used: 2 of 6 searches, no fetches.

result.reason: Duty is real. Lei 5/20 (27 Jan 2020) has specific obligations for lawyers, real estate activities, casinos and dealers (arts. ~37-44). It was amended by Lei 11/24 and Lei 8/26 (19 Aug 2026, in force on publication). FATF's June 2026 report still lists risk-based supervision of DNFBPs as open, but UIF says 98% of reports come from banks, so enforcement on small firms is weak. I found no reporting channel (goAML unconfirmed), no fine table for DNFBPs, and no competing local software. Unverified: notary-specific article, deadlines, register counts. Realistic buyers are small and unregulated, with low willingness to pay and no visible fines. Pain is mostly future.
